_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Gujarat State Fertilizers & Chemicals (consolidated, Rs crore). Segment-driven: Fertilizer products and Industrial products each grow revenue and earn an EBITDA margin (segment result + segment depreciation); central costs bridge to Screener EBITDA (other income excluded). Other income is built line by line (dividends from the listed stakes, interest on deposits, recurring items), not from a treasury yield, because the engine's treasury also holds the Rs4,610 cr investment book. Valued as a sum of the parts (street method): core business on EV/EBITDA, listed stakes at 30-Sep-2026 closes, unlisted stakes at Mar-26 fair value, net cash, less a holding discount derived from GSFC's own history.

segments.name: Fertilizer products
segments._why: FY27 +35%: Q1 fertiliser revenue +82% (Rs2,947 cr vs Rs1,619 cr) on volume +17% (5.26 lakh t) and realisation +56% (~Rs56,000/t vs ~Rs35,900/t) as DAP, APS and urea prices followed the Middle East cost spike and traded DAP rose; management budgets 'more than 22 lakh MT' for FY27 (FY26: 22.31 lakh t), so H2 growth is price, and the base gets tougher (FY26 realisations had already risen in H2). FY28 -8%: input prices and with them subsidy and MRPs ease if Middle East supply normalises; volume +2-3% with the C-Train able to swing between DAP and APS. FY29 +4%: volume and mix.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 5.8% (FY19), 6.5%, 7.8%, 12.7% (FY22), 17.6% (FY23 boom), 7.1%, 7.4%, 6.6% (FY26). Q1FY27 EBIT margin 4.09% vs 8.49% (EBITDA ~5.0%) as sulphur (+231% YoY), ammonia (+144%), gas (+38%) and P2O5 (+30%) outran prices on APS, AS and NPK; urea (New Urea Policy) and DAP (special package: import parity plus a 4% margin) are protected. Sulphur was still rising in August (Rs115,000/t vs Rs82,000/t Q1 average) and rabi NBS rates were not announced by 30-Sep: FY27 5.0%. FY28 6.5%, FY29 7.0%: back towards the FY24-26 average (7.0%) as sulphur normalises, not to the FY22-23 boom.

segments.name: Industrial products
segments._why: Caprolactam, nylon-6, melamine, methanol, MEK oxime, HX crystal, traded ammonia. FY27 +10%: Q1 +15% (Rs635 cr) on higher caprolactam sales and prices; melamine output was nil in Q1 (cheap Chinese imports; anti-dumping duty sought). FY28 +2% and FY29 +4%: capacity is fixed (caprolactam ~0.8 lakh t a year produced), so growth is price, set by Chinese supply.
segments._marginWhy: Segment EBITDA margin 19.8% (FY19), 1.1% (FY20), 12.0%, 20.9% (FY22), 3.7%, 4.5%, 6.7%, 12.1% (FY26): it follows the capro-benzene spread and Chinese melamine prices. Q1FY27 EBITDA ~22% on a $816/t spread (vs $540/t a year earlier); management expects the spread 'stable to soft' and melamine remains under import pressure. FY27 13.5% = Q1 plus ~11% for Q2-Q4; FY28-29 11%, close to the FY19-26 average (10.1%).

_unallocLabel: Central costs (sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA)
_unallocWhy: Sum of segment EBITDA less Screener EBITDA: Rs47 cr (FY19) to Rs103 cr (FY20); Rs58 cr, Rs76 cr, Rs56 cr, Rs66 cr in FY23-26 (unallocated expenses net of unallocated depreciation, plus the ~Rs24 cr of other income booked inside segment results). Q1FY27 unallocated costs were high (~Rs50 cr on the same bridge): Rs80 cr in FY27, then Rs75-78 cr.
_capexWhy: Cash capex Rs142 cr (FY23), Rs240 cr, Rs380 cr, Rs308 cr (FY26); segment capex Rs567 cr in FY26 incl. the Dahej land. FY27 Rs400 cr: C-Train APS modification (commissioning targeted Jul-Aug 2026), AS-I/AS-II refurbishment, maintenance (~Rs250 cr) and early payments on the Sikka phosphoric/sulphuric acid project (EPC award expected by Sep-2026). FY28-29 Rs800 cr each: the Sikka 600 TPD phosphoric acid + 1,800 TPD sulphuric acid project (cost not disclosed by 30-Sep-2026; we pencil in ~Rs1,100-1,200 cr, in line with Coromandel's similar-sized Kakinada acid plants) plus maintenance. The Dahej complex (276.7 ha leased Nov-2025) has no approved cost and is not in our numbers.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation Rs202 cr = 4.6% of average gross block (Rs4,413 cr); Q1FY27 Rs54 cr (Rs216 cr annualised). 4.2% gives ~Rs216 cr in FY27E rising to ~Rs275 cr in FY29E. The engine depreciates capex at once (CWIP held flat): the Sikka project would in reality start depreciating on commissioning (FY29 or later), so FY28-29 depreciation is slightly conservative.
_treasuryWhy: Not used: the engine's treasury includes the investment book (Rs4,610 cr at Mar-26, mostly listed shares), which earns dividends, not a yield. Interest on deposits is built inside other income.
_otherIncomeWhy: Built (AR FY26 note 30; Screener other income Rs287 cr FY26, TTM to Q1FY27 Rs277 cr). (1) Dividends from investments Rs130 cr a year (FY26 Rs106 cr): GNFC Rs21/share for FY26 x 2.92 cr shares = Rs61 cr (FY25: Rs18); Gujarat Energy (ex-Gujarat Gas) Rs8.90 x 4.77 cr shares = Rs42 cr (FY25 Rs5.82 on 4.69 cr); others (GIPCL, GACL, Indian Potash, Gujarat Chemical Port, banks) held at the FY26 residual of Rs26 cr; no growth assumed. (2) Interest: FY26 Rs143 cr (deposits Rs108 cr, advances Rs12 cr, others Rs23 cr); deposits of Rs1,160 cr at Mar-26 were used for working capital in Q1FY27 (Rs500 cr borrowed at Jun-26), so ~Rs67 cr in FY27, ~Rs42 cr in FY28 and ~Rs37 cr in FY29 as the Sikka project uses cash. (3) Recurring items (scrap, rent, insurance, write-backs, misc.) ~Rs27 cr (FY26 Rs27 cr). (4) Share of associates ~Rs11 cr (Screener counts it in other income). FY27E Rs235 cr is Rs52 cr below FY26: lower interest (-Rs76 cr) partly offset by higher dividends (+Rs24 cr).

otherTreasury.label: Deposits with financial institutions (in other current financial assets)
otherTreasury._why: Rs1,160 cr of deposits with financial institutions at Mar-26 sit in 'other current financial assets' (AR FY26 consolidated note 16), moved out of bank deposits (Rs1,622 cr at Mar-25). They are cash.

_interestWhy: FY26 Rs14 cr; Q1FY27 Rs10 cr with Rs500 cr of short-term borrowings at Jun-26 (DAP special-package subsidy arrives ~6 months after sale; inventory built for rabi). Rs35 cr in FY27; Rs40-50 cr as the Sikka project draws on cash and working-capital lines.
_taxWhy: Effective tax 22% in FY25-26 (FY26 incl. a Rs34 cr earlier-year credit; current tax Rs204 cr on PBT Rs861 cr = 24%); statutory 25.17%, less the deduction on dividends passed on. 24%.
_payoutWhy: DPS Rs10 (FY23), Rs4 (FY24), Rs5 (FY25), Rs5 (FY26) = 30-34% of EPS. Gujarat's 2023 PSU policy asks for the higher of 30% of profit or 5% of net worth (~Rs15/share), unless the Finance Department allows less for capex; GSFC has paid ~30% of profit. 30%.

dcf._betaWhy: A commodity producer with policy-set fertiliser margins and China-set chemical prices, no debt: market risk. Ke 12.5%; net cash, so the engine's use of Ke as the discount rate is appropriate.
dcf._tgWhy: Nominal growth of Indian fertiliser demand and chemical prices: 5%.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Revenue growth fades to 6% (volume ~2-3% plus inflation).
dcf._fadeMarginWhy: Consolidated EBITDA margin averaged 8.6% in FY19-26 (4.1% to 14.5%), boosted by the FY22-23 boom; 7.5% long-run.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Capex 3% of revenue long-run (FY19-26 average ~2.6%, plus backward integration); depreciation 2% of revenue.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Rabi NBS rates compensate the sulphur and ammonia spike and sulphur normalises in H2FY27; the capro-benzene spread holds near $700-800/t; the market keeps the lower holding discount it has applied since late 2024.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Sulphur stays above $800/t without compensating NBS rates, Chinese caprolactam and melamine capacity push spreads back to FY24-25 levels, the Sikka project costs more than planned, and the holding discount returns to its 2021-26 median as cash goes into capex rather than dividends or buybacks.

parts.name: Fertilizer products
parts.metricLabel: Sep-27E EBITDA (½ FY27E + ½ FY28E) × EV/EBITDA
parts.note: Core business at 6x trailing EBITDA at the target date: the low end of fertiliser peers on 30-Sep-2026 (Chambal 5.8x, NFL 6.1x, RCF 8.4x, Paradeep 9.2x) for a state-run, low-return business. The holding discount below is derived on the same 6x convention, so the choice largely nets out.

parts.name: Industrial products
parts.note: Same 6x: caprolactam, nylon-6 and melamine are commodity chemicals priced off China; margins have swung from 1% to 21% (FY20-26). Bull/bear cases move the EBITDA, not the multiple.

parts.name: Central costs
parts.note: Unallocated costs capitalised at the same multiple.

parts.name: GNFC: 2.92 cr shares (19.9%) at market
parts.note: AR FY26 note 7; unchanged after the Dec-2023 buyback.

parts.name: Gujarat Energy (ex-Gujarat Gas) + GSPL Transmission at market
parts.metricLabel: 4.77 cr Gujarat Energy shares × Rs237.58 + 1.59 cr GSPL Transmission shares × Rs144.40
parts.note: Includes 7.70 lakh shares received for GSPC (10:305) and 1 GSPL Transmission share per 3 Gujarat Energy shares (record date 2-Jul-2026).

parts.name: Other listed shares at market
parts.metricLabel: GACL 16.6 lakh × Rs618.85; Bandhan 11.4 lakh × Rs178.23; IDBI 5.5 lakh × Rs82.20; Paradeep 10.8 lakh × Rs154.28

parts.name: Unlisted shares at Mar-26 fair value
parts.metricLabel: Indian Potash Rs1,275 cr + Gujarat Chemical Port Rs242 cr + others Rs4 cr
parts.note: Company level-3 fair values (AR FY26 note 7/41).

parts.name: Associates at carrying value
parts.note: Gujarat Green Revolution, Karnalyte (impaired), Vadodara Enviro Channel.

parts.name: Less: investments at Mar-26 book (inside model net cash)
parts.metricLabel: Removes the Rs4,610 cr investment book counted in the model's cash and investments
parts.note: The holdings are valued separately above.

parts.name: Net cash at Sep-27E (model)
parts.metricLabel: ½ Mar-27E + ½ Mar-28E (cash, bank and FI deposits less borrowings, plus the investment book removed above)
parts.note: Mar-26: cash and bank Rs200 cr + FI deposits Rs1,160 cr - borrowings Rs27 cr = Rs1,333 cr; Rs500 cr borrowed at Jun-26 (seasonal).

parts.name: Less: holding discount
parts.note: Derived from GSFC's own discount to look-through value at 21 quarter-ends since Jun-2021 (see Valuation).

methods.name: Sum of the parts
methods.why: How the street has valued GSFC (Emkay's SOTP, the last full research series): listed and unlisted shares are ~90% of the market value on 30-Sep-2026, so the business and the portfolio are valued separately, less a holding discount derived from GSFC's own history.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Own one-year-forward P/E median since Apr-2021 (10.8x; trough years FY24, FY25 left out) less the 17% median P/E de-rating of fertiliser peers on 30-Sep-2026; bull = the median (no de-rating), bear = twice the de-rating. EPS includes dividends from the portfolio, so the market's usual discount is already inside the multiple.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: FCFF of the operating business FY28-37E (Ke 12.5%, terminal growth 5%) plus the model net cash at Mar-27E, which carries the investments at their Mar-26 book value with no discount.
